item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 23, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your latest media industry update.
The Federal Communications Commission has issued sixty thousand dollars in fines against three pirate radio operators in New York and Massachusetts. Each operator faces a twenty-thousand-dollar penalty. In Brooklyn, Henderson Lennox Elcock was fined for operating Wild FM on 106.3. In Spring Valley, New York, Etzer Toussaint was fined for operating Radio Telemodel on 88.9. And in Hyannis, Massachusetts, Shane Kelly was fined for operating a station called The Test on 87.9. Kelly requested leniency after shutting down his station, but the FCC upheld the penalty. The commission says unauthorized stations can interfere with licensed broadcasters and emergency alert transmissions. All three operators have thirty days to pay their fines.
In television news,
Television viewing declined 4.4 percent in August, according to Nielsen's latest report, as World Cup coverage ended and students headed back to school. Streaming continued to dominate, accounting for nearly half of all television viewing. YouTube reached a record 15.8 percent share, helped by increased viewing among adults 50 and older. Disney reclaimed second place among media distributors, while Netflix moved into third. Broadcast viewing dropped 14 percent, with ABC World News Tonight leading broadcast programs. Meanwhile, cable gained audience share as college football returned, with ESPN's North Carolina–TCU matchup topping cable telecasts. Nielsen also announced upcoming measurement changes, with September and October reports scheduled for release together later this year.
In public media news,
New York Public Radio has named Kimberly Watson its new Chief Development Officer. Watson will oversee fundraising, donor relations and membership growth for the organization, which operates WNYC, WQXR and WNYC Studios. She brings more than 30 years of experience working with major cultural institutions, including the Philadelphia Museum of Art and Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater. Her appointment comes as New York Public Radio expands its live events, digital initiatives and community engagement programs.
In music news,
The Country Music Association, Belmont University, Disney, and the Nashville Convention and Visitors Corporation have announced a combined one-million-dollar donation to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library. The gift follows a star-studded television tribute featuring Carrie Underwood, Reba McEntire, Lainey Wilson, Vince Gill, and other country stars. Parton founded the Imagination Library in 1995 to provide free books to young children. The program has now distributed more than 300 million books worldwide. The tribute special, *I Will Always Love You: A Celebration of Dolly Parton*, is streaming on Disney Plus and Hulu.
Turning to podcasts,
Triton Digital's September podcast rankings are out, and iHeart Audience Network continues to dominate, generating more than 67 million average weekly downloads. Audioboom ranked second with 15.5 million, followed by Cumulus Podcast Network, BBC and Salem Podcast Network. Among individual podcasts, *Stuff You Should Know* claimed the top spot, followed by *Pod Save America*, *My Favorite Murder*, *The Dan Bongino Show* and *The Bulwark Podcast*. The rankings measure downloads among participating publishers using industry-certified standards.
In media technology news,
Blackmagic Design has released two software updates for broadcast and video production equipment. Camera version 10.3.2 improves network control, switching between IP video and RAW workflows, and LUT functionality for the URSA Cine 12K LF. Converter Utility 12.4.1 delivers improvements and bug fixes for the company's 2110 IP Presentation Converter. Both updates are available through Blackmagic Design's support website.
Turning to radio,
Flor Leibaschoff has been named Chief Judge of the Radio Mercury Awards, which recognize excellence in radio and audio advertising. She's the Co-Founder and Chief Creative Officer of BeautifulBeast, with more than 25 years of industry experience. Leibaschoff made history as the first Hispanic female Chief Creative Officer in the United States. Her award-winning work has been recognized internationally, including at Cannes Lions and the Radio Mercury Awards. She calls the opportunity to lead judging for the 36-year-old competition a true honor.
And finally,
Apple has announced the first fully authorized Fleetwood Mac documentary, titled Fleetwood Mac: The Chain, premiering January 29th, 2027, on Apple TV. Directed by Frank Marshall, the film features interviews, rare footage and personal stories from the legendary band. The release celebrates the 50th anniversary of Rumours, one of rock music's most iconic albums.
For more media news, the latest jobs, free media tools and more, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
